National Lighthouse Day

images.alt:
National Lighthouse Day is observed in the United States each year on August 7th. The day honors the guidance, safety, and historical significance that lighthouses have provided for centuries along America's maritime coasts, lakes, and rivers.
Background:
• Historical Reason for the Date: August 7th commemorates the anniversary of the federal government's first public works act, signed by President George Washington on August 7, 1789, which allowed for the establishment and support of lighthouses, beacons, buoys, and public piers.
• Recognition: In 1989, the U.S. Congress officially designated August 7th as National Lighthouse Day to celebrate the bicentennial of the signing of the Lighthouse Act. 
Purpose and Celebration:
• Significance: The day recognizes the important role lighthouses have played in maritime safety, guiding ships sately to shore and standing as impressive historical structures.
• Celebrations: Many lighthouse preservation groups, museums, and local communities hold tours, festivals, and educational events to raise awareness about lighthouse history and preservation efforts.
